title: Priming, Persona, and Provocation: A Transferable Method for Behaviourally Auditing Conversational AI
content: Static benchmarks (fixed question sets scored one answer at a time) evaluate conversational artificial intelligence one prompt at a time, in one-off, no-memory conditions that no longer reflect how people actually use these systems. The most capable consumer assistants now carry persistent, cross-session memory, personalize to an inferred user, and are increasingly consulted for high-stakes emotional and health matters across sustained relationships. This paper presents a transferable method for behaviourally auditing conversational AI under exactly these conditions. The method is built from five components that are designed to travel together. Persona development constructs standardized personas that vary on sociodemographic and status dimensions, with internally consistent backstories. Memory priming seeds a model's personalization layer with persona backstory and relational history across preparatory sessions, before any test stimulus is delivered. Memory testing probes whether primed memory is retained, retrieved, and appropriately deployed across later sessions and agents. Persona vignettes deliver instrument-calibrated first-person scenarios in-character across graduated severity tiers. The adversarial narrative audit runs escalating storylines in isolated ghost chats and reports results only at susceptibility-category level. We situate the method within the algorithm-audit, red-teaming, and standardized-patient traditions, and we state the contract that any scoring layer must satisfy in order to attach, so that the method remains agnostic to both domain and instrument. We address validity under small-n, hypothesis-generating designs, model non-determinism, and version drift, and we close with a procedure for adapting the method to new applications. The method was developed and applied in a completed audit of four commercial conversational systems in a mental health setting, whose case reports are in preparation; that audit serves here only as the worked example, and nothing in the architecture depends on its setting.
